CBS Corp.&#8217;s certificate of incorporation contains provisions related to corporate opportunities that may be of interest to both the Company and Viacom Inc. CBS Corp.&#8217;s certificate of incorporation provides that in the event that a director, officer or controlling stockholder of the Company who is also a director, officer or controlling stockholder of Viacom Inc. acquires knowledge of a potential corporate opportunity for both the Company and Viacom Inc., such director, officer or controlling stockholder may present such opportunity to the Company or Viacom Inc. or both, as such director, officer or controlling stockholder deems appropriate in his or her sole discretion, and that by doing so such person will have satisfied his or her fiduciary duties to the Company and its stockholders. In addition, CBS Corp.&#8217;s certificate of incorporation provides that the Company renounces any interest in any such opportunity presented to Viacom Inc. Furthermore, CBS Corp.&#8217;s certificate of incorporation provides that neither the Company nor Viacom Inc. has any duty to refrain from engaging in the same or similar activities or lines of business as the other corporation, doing business with any potential or actual customer or supplier of the other corporation, or employing or soliciting for employment any officer or employee of the other corporation, and that no officer or director of either corporation shall be liable to the other corporation or the other corporation&#8217;s stockholders for breach of any fiduciary duty by reason of any such activities of the Company or Viacom Inc., as the case may be. These provisions create the possibility that a corporate opportunity of one of such companies may be used for the benefit of the other company. As announced on August 1, 2018, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors (&#8220;Board&#8221;) retained two law firms to conduct a full investigation of the allegations in recent press reports about the Company&#8217;s former Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Leslie Moonves, CBS News and cultural issues at all levels of the Company. The Company is cooperating with these inquiries.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">On August 27, 2018 and on October 1, 2018, each of Gene Samit and John Lantz, respectively, filed putative class action suits in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, individually and on behalf of others similarly situated, for claims that are similar to those alleged in the amended complaint described below.&#160; On November 6, 2018, the Court entered an order consolidating the two actions.&#160; On November 30, 2018, the Court appointed Construction Laborers Pension Trust for Southern California as the lead plaintiff of the consolidated action.&#160; On February 11, 2019, the lead plaintiff filed a consolidated amended putative class action complaint against the Company, certain current and former senior executives and members of the Board.&#160; The consolidated action is stated to be on behalf of purchasers of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock between September 26, 2016 and December 4, 2018.&#160; This action seeks to recover damages arising during this time period allegedly caused by the defendants&#8217; purported violations of the federal securities laws, including by allegedly making materially false and misleading statements or failing to disclose material information, and seeks costs and expenses as well as remedies under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder.&#160; </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Separation Agreement</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.    On September 9, 2018, the Company entered into a separation and settlement agreement and releases (the &#8220;Separation Agreement&#8221;) with Mr. Leslie Moonves, pursuant to which Mr. Moonves resigned as a director and as Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company. Pursuant to the Separation Agreement, the Company is contributing the aggregate amount of $20 million toward various charitable organizations that support the #MeToo movement and equality for women in the workplace, which organizations were mutually agreed by the Company and Mr. Moonves. The Company has recorded the contribution of $20 million in &#8220;Restructuring and other corporate matters&#8221; on the Consolidated Statements of Operations for the year ended December 31, 2018. In October 2018, the Company contributed $120 million to a grantor trust. On December 17, 2018, the Board announced that, following its consideration of the findings of the investigation referred to above, it had determined that there were grounds to terminate Mr. Moonves&#8217;s employment for cause under his employment agreement with the Company. Any dispute related to the Board&#8217;s determination is subject to binding arbitration as set forth in the Separation Agreement. On January 16, 2019, Mr. Moonves notified the Company of his election to demand binding arbitration with respect to this matter and the related Board investigation. The assets of the grantor trust will remain in the trust until a final determination in the arbitration. The Company is currently unable to determine the </span></div><div><br/></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">I-</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">28</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:right;text-indent:576px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> </span></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">outcome of the arbitration and the amount, if any, that may be awarded thereunder and, accordingly, no accrual for this matter has been made in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Claims Related to Former Businesses: Asbestos.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">   The Company is a defendant in lawsuits claiming various personal injuries related to asbestos and other materials, which allegedly occurred as a result of exposure caused by various products manufactured by Westinghouse, a predecessor, generally prior to the early 1970s. Westinghouse was neither a producer nor a manufacturer of asbestos. The Company is typically named as one of a large number of defendants in both state and federal cases. In the majority of asbestos lawsuits, the plaintiffs have not identified which of the Company&#8217;s products is the basis of a claim. Claims against the Company in which a product has been identified most commonly relate to allegations of exposure to asbestos-containing insulating material used in conjunction with turbines.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Claims are frequently filed and/or settled in groups, which may make the amount and timing of settlements, and the number of pending claims, subject to significant fluctuation from period to period. The Company does not report as pending those claims on inactive, stayed, deferred or similar dockets that some jurisdictions have established for claimants who allege minimal or no impairment. As of December&#160;31, 2018, the Company had pending approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">31,570</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> asbestos claims, as compared with approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">31,660</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> as of December 31, 2017 and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">33,610</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> as of December&#160;31, 2016. During 2018, the Company received approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">3,290</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> new claims and closed or moved to an inactive docket approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">3,380</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> claims. The Company reports claims as closed when it becomes aware that a dismissal order has been entered by a court or when the Company has reached agreement with the claimants on the material terms of a settlement. Settlement costs depend on the seriousness of the injuries that form the basis of the claims, the quality of evidence supporting the claims and other factors. The Company&#8217;s total costs for the years 2018 and 2017 for settlement and defense of asbestos claims after insurance recoveries and net of tax were approximately $</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">45 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and $</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">57 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, respectively. The Company&#8217;s costs for settlement and defense of asbestos claims may vary year to year and insurance proceeds are not always recovered in the same period as the insured portion of the expenses.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Filings include claims for individuals suffering from mesothelioma, a rare cancer, the risk of which is allegedly increased by exposure to asbestos; lung cancer, a cancer which may be caused by various factors, one of which is alleged to be asbestos exposure; other cancers, and conditions that are substantially less serious, including claims brought on behalf of individuals who are asymptomatic as to an allegedly asbestos-related disease. The predominant number of pending claims against the Company are non-cancer claims. The Company believes that its reserves and insurance are adequate to cover its asbestos liabilities. This belief is based upon many factors and assumptions, including the number of outstanding claims, estimated average cost per claim, the breakdown of claims by disease type, historic claim filings, costs per claim of resolution and the filing of new claims. While the number of asbestos claims filed against the Company has remained generally flat in recent years, it is difficult to predict future asbestos liabilities, as events and circumstances may occur, including, among others, the number and types of claims and average cost to resolve such claims, which could affect the Company&#8217;s estimate of its asbestos liabilities.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Other.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">    The Company from time to time receives claims from federal and state environmental regulatory agencies and other entities asserting that it is or may be liable for environmental cleanup costs and related damages principally relating to historical and predecessor operations of the Company. In addition, the Company from time to time receives personal injury claims including toxic tort and product liability claims (other than asbestos) arising from historical operations of the Company and its predecessors. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div><a id="s57B81545E2F943E755A6F02BD51A6D9C"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&#160;4.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Mine Safety Disclosures.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Not applicable.</span></div><div style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div><a id="s3693DB4834EBBE326BC6F02BA54A6270"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Overview</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Business Overview and Strategy</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The Company operates businesses which span the media and entertainment industries, including the CBS Television Network, cable networks, content production and distribution, television stations, direct-to-consumer digital streaming services and other internet-based businesses, and consumer publishing. The Company&#8217;s principal strategy is to create and acquire premium content that is widely accepted by audiences and generate affiliate and subscription fee, licensing and advertising revenues from the distribution of this content on multiple media platforms and to various geographic locations. The Company plans to increase its investment in premium content to enhance its opportunities for revenue growth, which include exhibiting the Company&#8217;s content on its direct-to-consumer digital streaming services; expanding the distribution of its content internationally; and securing compensation from multichannel video programming distributors (&#8220;MVPDs&#8221;), third-party live television digital streaming offerings (&#8220;virtual MVPDs&#8221;), and television stations affiliated with the CBS Television Network. The Company also seeks to grow its advertising revenues by monetizing all content viewership as industry measurements evolve to reflect viewers&#8217; changing habits. The Company&#8217;s continued ability to capitalize on these and other emerging opportunities will provide incremental revenues across all of the Company&#8217;s main revenue streams.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Corporate Matters</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">In August 2018, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors (the &#8220;Board&#8221;) retained two law firms to conduct a full investigation of allegations in recent press reports about the Company&#8217;s former Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Leslie Moonves, CBS News and cultural issues at all levels of the Company. In September 2018, Mr. Moonves resigned as a director and as Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, pursuant to a separation and settlement agreement and releases, and the Company appointed its then Chief Operating Officer, Mr. Joseph R. Ianniello, as President and Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Company. The Board is conducting a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and Mr. Ianniello is a candidate in this search. On December 17, 2018, the Board announced the completion of the investigation and certain findings of the investigation. Also during 2018, the Company was involved in legal proceedings with its controlling shareholder, National Amusements, Inc., among others, which concluded with the dismissal of all claims pursuant to a settlement and release agreement. Pursuant to this agreement, on September 9, 2018, seven members of the Board resigned and the Board appointed six new members to the Board. On September 23, 2018, two directors who had served as members of the Board prior to September 9, 2018 resigned to pursue other interests, and, on October 21, 2018, another director resigned for health-related reasons. In addition, in early 2018, a potential combination with Viacom Inc. was evaluated by a special committee established by the Board. The uncertainties arising from leadership changes at the Company may have an adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business. In connection with the aforementioned matters, the Company incurred expenses of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$128 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in 2018. See &#8220;Legal Matters&#8221; for certain related information.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span Advertising revenues grew </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">8%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, driven by record political advertising sales from the 2018 midterm elections and the Company&#8217;s acquisition of Network 10 in the fourth quarter of 2017. During </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the Company experienced strong demand for CBS Television Network advertising. Underlying CBS Television Network advertising revenues in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> were comparable with </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, as higher pricing and higher ratings for Sunday National Football League (&#8220;NFL&#8221;) games were offset by lower ratings for the Company&#8217;s primetime programming. Affiliate and subscription fees increased </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">7%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, driven by </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">62%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> growth from the Company&#8217;s direct-to-consumer digital streaming services, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">CBS All Access</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Showtime</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, and higher station affiliation fees and retransmission revenues, including from virtual MVPDs. These increases were partially offset by Showtime Networks&#8217; distribution of the Floyd Mayweather/Conor McGregor pay-per-view boxing event in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, which reduced the affiliate and subscription fee comparison by </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">eight</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> percentage points. Content licensing and distribution revenues were up </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">3%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, mainly from higher international licensing and the adoption of a new revenue recognition standard in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. This new standard resulted in revenues from the distribution of third-party content now being recognized based on the gross amount of consideration received from the customer, with an offsetting increase to participation expenses (see &#8220;Adoption of New Revenue Standard&#8221;). These increases were partially offset by lower domestic licensing compared with </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. The net earnings comparison was impacted by the following discrete items: the reversal of a valuation allowance in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, charges in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> resulting from a pension settlement and the enactment of federal tax legislation in December </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> (the &#8220;Tax Reform Act&#8221;); and, in discontinued operations for </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, a net loss from the split-off of CBS Radio Inc. (&#8220;CBS Radio&#8221;) and a noncash charge to adjust the carrying value of CBS Radio. id="sfc3febe731b74222879b7db894d6d006"></a></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:6pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:6pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:6pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:6pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">(Tabular dollars in millions, except per share amounts)</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Adoption of New Revenue Standard</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">During the first quarter of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the Company adopted Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) Accounting Standards Codification 606 (&#8220;ASC 606&#8221;) on the recognition of revenues which primarily resulted in two changes to the Company&#8217;s revenue recognition policies. </span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-bottom:10px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:60px;"></td><td></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:36px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Revenues from Distribution Arrangements</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;padding-left:60px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Revenues from the Company&#8217;s distribution of third-party content are now recognized based on the gross amount of consideration received from the customer, with an offsetting participation expense recognized for the fees paid to the third party. Under previous accounting guidance, such revenues, which include content licensing and distribution revenues and advertising revenues, were recognized at the net amount retained by the Company after the payment of fees to the third party. For the year ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, revenues and operating expenses relating to such distribution arrangements were each </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$279 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> higher under ASC 606 than the amounts that would have been reported under previous accounting guidance, with no impact to operating income. </span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-bottom:10px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:60px;"></td><td></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:36px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Revenues from the Renewal of Licensing Agreements</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;padding-left:60px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Revenues associated with the renewal of an existing license agreement are now recognized at the beginning of the renewal period. Under previous accounting guidance, these revenues were recognized upon the execution of such renewal. Content licensing and distribution revenue comparisons will continue to be impacted by fluctuations resulting from the timing of when Company-owned television series are made available for multiyear licensing agreements. Therefore, this change is not expected to have a material impact on the trend of the Company&#8217;s financial results. Additionally, historically, on an annual basis, revenues from renewals executed each year have approximated revenues associated with renewal periods that began in the same year. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The Company applied the modified retrospective method of adoption and therefore, prior periods continue to be presented under previous accounting guidance. The following table presents the Company&#8217;s revenues, operating income, net earnings from continuing operations, and diluted EPS from continuing operations, as well as the corresponding year-over-year comparisons, as if results for the year ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> were recognized under ASC 606. These amounts are non-GAAP financial measures and are reconciled below to the most directly comparable financial measures in accordance with GAAP. The Company believes that presenting its financial results for 2017 under ASC 606 is relevant and useful for investors because it allows investors to view results for 2017 on a basis consistent with the 2018 presentation, and makes it easier to compare the Company&#8217;s year-over-year results. If revenues were recognized under ASC 606 for 2017, the year-over-year comparisons to 2018 for operating income, net earnings from continuing operations and diluted EPS from continuing operations would have been similar to the comparisons on a reported basis.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><div style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">8%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">increase</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in advertising revenues was driven by the Company&#8217;s acquisition of Network 10 in the fourth quarter of 2017 and record political advertising sales in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> associated with the U.S. midterm elections. Underlying CBS Television Network advertising revenues for </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> were comparable with </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, as higher pricing and higher ratings for Sunday NFL games were offset by lower ratings for the Company&#8217;s primetime programming.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Advertising revenues for </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> also benefited from higher revenues from the distribution of third-party content, resulting from such revenues now being recognized at the gross amount of consideration received from the customer, with an offsetting increase to operating expenses, as a result of the adoption of a new revenue recognition standard (see &#8220;Adoption of New Revenue Standard&#8221;). Under previous guidance such distribution revenues were recognized at the net amount retained by the Company after the payment of fees to the third party. These increases were partially offset by the absence of the broadcast of five </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Thursday Night Football </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">games and the National Semifinals and National Championship games of the NCAA Tournament, which were broadcast on the CBS Television Network in 2017. The National Semifinals and National Championship games of the NCAA Tournament are broadcast by the CBS Television Network every other year through 2032 under the current agreements with the NCAA and Turner Broadcasting System, Inc. (&#8220;Turner&#8221;). </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">In </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, advertising revenues will benefit from the CBS Television Network&#8217;s broadcast of the Super Bowl, which airs on the CBS Television Network on a rotating basis with other networks through 2022 under the current contract with the NFL, and the National Semifinals and National Championship games of the NCAA Tournament. However, the advertising revenue comparison in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> will be negatively affected by the benefit in 2018 from record political advertising sales. The CBS Television Network&#8217;s upfront advertising sales (&#8220;Upfront&#8221;) for the 2018/2019 television broadcast season, which runs from the middle of September 2018 through the middle of September 2019, resulted in pricing and volume increases compared with the prior broadcast season, which are expected to benefit the Company&#8217;s advertising revenues during the 2018/2019 broadcast season. (See page I-2 for a description of the Upfront market.) However, overall advertising revenues for the Company will be dependent on ratings for its programming and market conditions, including demand in the scatter advertising market, in which advertisers purchase the remaining advertising spots closer to the broadcast of the related programming.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Content Licensing and Distribution</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Content licensing and distribution revenues are principally comprised of fees from the licensing of internally-produced television programming; fees from the distribution of third-party programming; and revenues from the publishing and distribution of consumer books. For </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, content licensing and distribution revenues increased </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">3%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, benefiting from higher revenues from the distribution of third-party content, resulting from such revenues now being recognized at the gross amount of consideration received from the customer, with an offsetting increase to participation expense, as a result of the adoption of a new revenue recognition standard (see &#8220;Adoption of New Revenue Standard&#8221;). Under previous guidance such distribution revenues were recognized at the net amount retained by the Company after the payment of fees to the third party. Content licensing and distribution revenues also reflected growth in international licensing, offset by lower domestic licensing, mainly resulting from several large sales in 2017, including </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">NCIS: New Orleans</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Madam Secretary</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and titles from the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">CSI</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> franchise.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Content licensing and distribution revenue comparisons are impacted by fluctuations resulting from the timing of the availability of Company-owned television series for multiyear licensing agreements. Television license fee revenues are recognized at the beginning of the license period in which programs are made available to the licensee for exhibition. Unrecognized revenues attributable to signed license agreements for produced programming that is not yet available for exhibition were </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$1.08 billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> at </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$670 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> at </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, </span></div><div><br/></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">II-</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">10</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:6pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:6pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:6pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:6pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">which increased to $1.33 billion on January 1, 2018 upon the adoption of ASC 606. At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the Company had approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">800</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> episodes of scripted original programming that had not yet been made available in the secondary domestic marketplace (See page II-59 for a description of the secondary marketplace).</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Total outstanding receivables attributable to revenues recognized under licensing agreements were </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$3.57 billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> at </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$4.06 billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> at </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$3.45 billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> at January 1, 2018. At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the total amount due from these receivables was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$1.96 billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$771 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$430 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2021</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2022</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$181 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2023</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and thereafter. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Affiliate and Subscription Fees</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Affiliate and subscription fees are principally comprised of revenues received from MVPDs and virtual MVPDs for carriage of the Company&#8217;s cable networks (&#8220;cable affiliate fees&#8221;), as well as fees received from television stations affiliated with the CBS Television Network (&#8220;station affiliation fees&#8221;); fees for authorizing the MVPDs&#8217; and virtual MVPDs&#8217; carriage of the Company&#8217;s owned television stations (&#8220;retransmission fees&#8221;); subscription fees for the Company&#8217;s direct-to-consumer digital streaming services; and revenues received for the distribution of pay-per-view boxing events. For </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">7%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">increase</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in affiliate and subscription fees reflects </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">22%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> growth in station affiliation and retransmission fees and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">62%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> growth from the Company&#8217;s direct-to-consumer digital streaming services, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">CBS All Access</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Showtime</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. These increases were partially offset by Showtime Networks&#8217; distribution of the Floyd Mayweather/Conor McGregor pay-per-view boxing event in 2017, which reduced the comparison by </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">eight</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> percentage points.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Over the next two years, agreements with MVPDs and virtual MVPDs, representing approximately 85% of the Company&#8217;s total subscribers to these services, and agreements with station affiliates representing approximately 60% of the Company&#8217;s total subscribers under its station affiliation agreements, will come up for renewal. Historically, renewals of these agreements have resulted in increases in the rates received by the Company and therefore, the Company expects to benefit from these renewals over the next few years. In addition, the Company&#8217;s existing agreements with station affiliates, MVPDs and virtual MVPDs include annual contractual increases. Together, these factors are expected to result in continued growth in affiliate and subscription fees over the next several years.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Other </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Other revenues are principally comprised of revenues from the rental of production facilities and ancillary digital revenues.  </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">International Revenues</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">For </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, international revenues increased </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">26%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> primarily driven by the Company&#8217;s acquisition of Network 10 in the fourth quarter of 2017. The Company generated approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">17%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">15%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of its total revenues from international regions in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018 and 2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, respectively. </span></div><div For </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">18%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">increase</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in production expenses reflected an increased investment in content, including a 17% increase in the number of series produced for distribution on multiple platforms, and the acquisition of Network 10 in the fourth quarter of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">During the fourth quarter of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, in connection with recent management changes, the Company implemented changes to its programming strategy, primarily at CBS Films, which will shift its focus from theatrical films to developing content for the Company&#8217;s direct-to-consumer digital streaming services. As a result, the Company recorded programming charges of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$85 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Participation, Distribution and Royalty</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Participation, distribution and royalty costs primarily include participation and residual expenses for television programming, royalty costs for Publishing content and other distribution expenses incurred with respect to television content, such as print and advertising. For </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">30%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">increase</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in participation, distribution and royalty costs was primarily driven by the adoption of new revenue recognition guidance, which resulted in revenues from the Company&#8217;s distribution of third-party content now being recognized based on the gross amount of consideration received from the customer, with an offsetting participation expense recognized for the fees paid to the third party. Under previous accounting guidance, such revenues were recognized at the net amount retained by the Company after the payment of fees to the third party. This change resulted in an increase to both revenues and participation expenses of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$279 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, with no impact to the Company&#8217;s operating income. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span mainly reflected higher costs associated with growth in the Company&#8217;s direct-to-consumer digital streaming services and expenses of Network 10, which was acquired in the fourth quarter of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">, in connection with the preparation of its 2017 federal tax return, the Company As a result, during the third quarter of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">, the Company established a deferred tax liability associated with this deduction at the 2017 federal tax rate of 35%, and concurrently recorded a net tax benefit of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">$69 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">, primarily reflecting the re-measurement of this deferred tax liability at the reduced federal corporate tax rate of 21% under the Tax Reform Act. style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">9%</span><span primarily reflects the benefit to 2016 from CBS&#8217;s broadcast of the Super Bowl, which is broadcast on the CBS Television Network on a rotating basis with other networks. The decline also reflects the benefit in 2016 from political advertising sales during the 2016 Presidential election cycle. Underlying CBS Television Network advertising revenues declined </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, mainly as a result of lower ratings for the Company&#8217;s programming, which was partially offset by higher pricing. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Content Licensing and Distribution</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">For </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">8%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">increase</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in content licensing and distribution revenues reflected growth in both international and domestic licensing sales. The increase in domestic licensing sales was primarily driven by sales of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">NCIS: New Orleans</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Madam Secretary</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and several titles from the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">CSI </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">franchise. As a result of this tax law, the Company recorded a net provisional charge of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">$129 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"> for the year ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">, reflecting an estimated tax impact of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">$407 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"> on the Company&#8217;s historical accumulated foreign earnings and profits, partially offset by an estimated benefit of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">$278 million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"> to adjust the Company&#8217;s deferred income tax balances as a result of the reduction in the federal corporate income tax rate from </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">35%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">21%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:4px;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;text-indent:-18px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">(b)  Reflects excess tax benefits associated with the exercise of stock options and vesting of RSUs. During the first quarter of 2017, the Company adopted FASB guidance which requires that the difference between the tax benefit from stock-based compensation expense and the deduction on the tax return be recognized within the income tax provision on the statement of operations. Previously, such difference was recognized in stockholders&#8217; equity on the balance sheet. This difference occurs because stock-based compensation expense is determined based on the grant-date fair value of the award, whereas the tax deduction is based on the fair value on the date the stock option is exercised or the RSU vests. This guidance requires the income statement classification to be applied prospectively, and therefore, excess tax benefits for prior periods remain classified in stockholders&#8217; equity.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:4px;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;text-indent:-18px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">(c)  For the year ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">, primarily reflects tax benefits from the resolution of certain state income tax matters. Free cash flow reflects the Company&#8217;s net cash flow provided by (used for) operating activities before operating cash flow from discontinued operations, and less capital expenditures; and adjusted free cash flow reflects the Company&#8217;s net cash flow provided by (used for) operating activities before operating cash flow from discontinued operations and discretionary contributions to prefund the Company&#8217;s pension plans, and less capital expenditures. The Company&#8217;s calculations of free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow include capital expenditures because investment in capital expenditures is a use of cash that is directly related to the Company&#8217;s operations. Adjusted free cash flow excludes discretionary contributions to prefund the Company&#8217;s pension plans because management assesses the Company&#8217;s ability to generate operating cash flows without considering the impact from discretionary pension contributions, and decisions regarding the timing of pension plan funding are not dependent on the level of operating cash flows generated during the period. The Company&#8217;s net cash flow provided by (used for) operating activities is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div><br/></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">II-</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">35</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:6pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:6pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:6pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:6pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Results of Operations and Financial Condition (Continued)</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">(Tabular dollars in millions, except per share amounts)</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Management believes free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow provide investors with an important perspective on the cash available to the Company to service debt, make strategic acquisitions and investments, maintain its capital assets, satisfy its tax obligations, and fund ongoing operations and working capital needs. As a result, free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow are significant measures of the Company&#8217;s ability to generate long-term value. It is useful for investors to know whether this ability is being enhanced or degraded as a result of the Company&#8217;s operating performance. The Company believes the presentation of free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow is relevant and useful for investors because it allows investors to evaluate the cash generated from the Company&#8217;s underlying operations in a manner similar to the method used by management. Free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow are among several components of incentive compensation targets for certain management personnel. In addition, free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow are primary measures used externally by the Company&#8217;s investors, analysts and industry peers for purposes of valuation and comparison of the Company&#8217;s operating performance to other companies in its industry.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">As free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow are not measures calculated in accordance with GAAP, free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow should not be considered in isolation of, or as a substitute for, either net cash flow provided by (used for) operating activities as a measure of liquidity or net earnings (loss) as a measure of operating performance. Free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow, as the Company calculates them, may not be comparable to similarly titled measures employed by other companies. In addition, free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow as measures of liquidity have certain limitations, do not necessarily represent funds available for discretionary use and are not necessarily measures of the Company&#8217;s ability to fund its cash needs. When comparing free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow to net cash flow provided by (used for) operating activities, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, users of this financial information should consider the types of events and transactions that are not reflected in free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The following table presents a reconciliation of the Company&#8217;s net cash flow provided by operating activities to free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><div The Company, at its option, may also borrow in certain foreign currencies up to specified limits under the Credit Facility. Borrowing rates under the Credit Facility are determined at the Company&#8217;s option at the time of each borrowing and are based generally on the prime rate in the U.S. or LIBOR plus a margin based on the Company&#8217;s senior unsecured debt rating. The Company pays a facility fee based on the total amount of the commitments.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The Credit Facility requires the Company to maintain a maximum Consolidated Leverage Ratio of 4.5x at the end of each quarter as further described in the Credit Facility. At December&#160;31, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Leverage Ratio was approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">3.1x</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The Consolidated Leverage Ratio reflects the ratio of the Company&#8217;s indebtedness from continuing operations, adjusted to exclude certain capital lease obligations, at the end of a quarter, to the Company&#8217;s Consolidated EBITDA for the trailing four consecutive quarters.&#160; Consolidated EBITDA is defined in the Credit Facility as operating income plus interest income and before depreciation, amortization and certain other noncash items.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The Credit Facility is used for general corporate purposes. The Company&#8217;s operating needs include, among other items, commitments for sports programming rights, television and film programming, talent contracts, operating leases, interest payments, and pension funding obligations. The Company&#8217;s investing and financing spending includes capital expenditures, share repurchases, dividends and principal payments on its outstanding indebtedness. The Company believes that its operating cash flows, cash and cash equivalents, borrowing capacity under its Credit Facility, which had </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.49 billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of remaining availability at December&#160;31, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, and access to capital markets are sufficient to fund its operating, investing and financing requirements for the next twelve months.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The Company&#8217;s funding for short-term and long-term obligations will come primarily from cash flows from operating activities. Any additional cash funding requirements are financed with short-term borrowings, including commercial paper, and long-term debt. To the extent that commercial paper is not available to the Company, the existing Credit Facility provides sufficient capacity to satisfy short-term borrowing needs. The Company routinely assesses its capital structure and opportunistically enters into transactions to lower its interest expense, which could result in a charge from the early extinguishment of debt.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Funding for the Company&#8217;s long-term debt obligations due over the next five years of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.63 billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> is expected to come from the Company&#8217;s ability to refinance its debt and cash generated from operating activities.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">At December 31, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the Company had </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.46 billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of remaining availability under its share repurchase program. long-term debt. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span
